{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation yielded the highest success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.562 s), with strong Path Efficiency (0.502) and highest Average Speed (12.83 cm/s)",
    "Bright Visual Only performed comparably to Combined on Success (0.785) and Time-to-Target (2.614 s), with slightly lower Path Efficiency (0.504) and Average Speed (12.68 cm/s)",
    "Dim Visual Only showed intermediate performance: Success 0.673, Time-to-Target 3.140 s, Path Efficiency 0.434, Average Speed 11.97 cm/s",
    "ICMS Only was similar to Dim Visual Only: Success 0.685, Time-to-Target 3.053 s, Path Efficiency 0.432, Average Speed 12.04 cm/s",
    "Sham stimulation produced markedly inferior performance across all metrics: lowest Success (0.273), slowest Time-to-Target (4.682 s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74 cm/s), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Angular Dispersion was highest in Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual Only (0.387), intermediate in ICMS Only (0.354), lower in Dim Visual Only (0.336), and lowest in Sham (0.236)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined (0.780) and Bright Visual Only (0.785) shows a 2.9-fold difference, the largest effect across any metric",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.682 s) was 1.83× slower than Combined (2.562 s), representing a 2.12 s absolute difference",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502) shows a 63% relative deficit",
    "Average Speed: Sham (10.74 cm/s) was 16.3% slower than Combined (12.83 cm/s), a smaller but consistent deficit",
    "AD: Sham (0.236) versus Combined (0.399) shows a 69% relative reduction, suggesting more directed movement in the absence of stimulation"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Multisensory and unisensory visual stimulation substantially improve navigation performance compared to no stimulation. The Combined and Bright Visual Only paradigms produce nearly equivalent high performance, suggesting that bright visual cues alone may be sufficient for optimal behavior. Dim visual cues and ICMS alone provide intermediate benefit, while sham stimulation results in poor performance characterized by slow, inefficient, unsuccessful trials with straighter trajectories (lower AD). The pattern suggests sensory substitution or augmentation is critical for this navigation task, with visual information appearing more influential than ICMS alone. The higher AD in stimulated conditions may reflect active exploration or sensory-driven orienting behaviors that support target localization.",
  "limitations": [
    "No statistical tests (ANOVA, post-hoc comparisons) are provided to assess significance of between-group differences",
    "Unequal sample sizes across paradigms (Combined n=48,846 versus Sham n=3,505) may affect precision of estimates",
    "No information on within-mouse variability or mouse-level random effects",
    "Cannot determine if Combined stimulation provides additive benefit over Bright Visual Only alone without formal interaction testing",
    "No temporal or learning effects are characterized—data may mix early and late training performance",
    "Path Efficiency values >1 in some conditions (max 29.8 overall) suggest possible measurement artifacts or outliers not excluded",
    "Causal claims about stimulation efficacy are limited without proper control for order effects or counterbalancing"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects regression with Mouse as random intercept to account for within-subject clustering, followed by planned contrasts comparing Combined versus Bright Visual Only (equivalence test), Combined versus ICMS Only + Dim Visual Only (interaction test for multisensory integration), and all stimulated conditions versus Sham (dunnett-style). Additionally, visualize distributions and examine trial-level correlations among the five metrics to characterize performance trade-offs."
}
